```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4)
invisible(Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "en_US.UTF-8"))  # else cat() writes non-ASCII as <U+2010> under the C locale
library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(stringr); library(readr); library(ggplot2); library(knitr); library(here)
source(here("R", "profile.R"))   # PROFILE_VERSION (set by R/08_render_site.R): which profile's files to read
V  <- profile_version()
rd <- \(f) read_csv(proc_path(f), show_col_types = FALSE)
E  <- params$engine
eng      <- rd("engines.csv") |> filter(engine_name == E) |> mutate(award_id = as.character(award_id))
m        <- rd("metrics_engine.csv") |> filter(engine_name == E)
people   <- rd("people_roles_evidence.csv") |> filter(engine_name == E, in_team)
partners <- rd("partners.csv") |> filter(engine_name == E)
profile  <- if (V == "v1") rd("tech_profile.csv") |> filter(engine_name == E) else
  rd("tech_profile_v3_1_core.csv") |> filter(engine_name == E)
pyear    <- rd("metrics_patents_year.csv") |> filter(engine_name == E)
wyear    <- rd("metrics_papers_year.csv") |> filter(engine_name == E)
lq       <- rd("metrics_lq_cpc.csv") |> filter(engine_name == E)
top_asg  <- rd("metrics_top_assignees.csv") |> filter(engine_name == E)
pe       <- rd("patents_engine.csv") |> filter(engine_name == E)
wi       <- rd("works_institutions.csv") |> filter(engine_name == E)
wp       <- rd("works_people.csv") |> filter(engine_name == E)
pt       <- read_csv(proc_path("patents_team.csv"),
                     col_types = cols(patent_id = col_character(), .default = col_guess())) |> filter(engine_name == E)
people   <- people |>
  left_join(wp |> group_by(person_id) |> summarise(n_listed = n(), n_topic = sum(in_engine_topics, na.rm = TRUE)),
            by = "person_id") |>
  left_join(pt |> group_by(person_id) |> summarise(n_pat = n_distinct(patent_id),
                                                  n_pat_profile = n_distinct(patent_id[in_tech_profile])),
            by = "person_id")
na0 <- \(x) ifelse(is.na(x), 0, x)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
```

**`r eng$title`**, led by `r eng$lead_org`. NSF award [`r eng$award_id`](https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=`r eng$award_id`), start `r format(eng$start_date, "%B %Y")`. Search window for papers and patents: from `r format(as.Date(eng$window_from), "%B %Y")` (five years before the award) onward.

## At a glance

```{r glance}
tibble(
  Measure = c("People named by NSF or the Engine's site", "of them active researchers (>= 5 works since window start)",
              "Team members who are inventors (2021-2025 grants, in the region)",
              "Partners (site list + team members' organisations)", "Knowledge-producer partners (universities, labs, institutes)",
              "Partner papers in the Engine's topics", "of them with an in-region partner",
              "Regional patents in the technology profile (2021-2025 grants)",
              "Location quotient of the technology profile (patents)",
              "Share of regional technology patents owned by partners"),
  Value = c(m$team, m$active_researchers, m$team_inventors, m$partners, m$knowledge_producers,
            na0(m$partner_works_in_topics), na0(m$partner_works_in_topics_region), m$pat_region_tech,
            m$lq_profile, scales::percent(m$share_region_tech_by_partners, accuracy = 0.1))
) |> kable(align = c("l", "r"))
```

## Economic base

```{r economy}
econ <- rd("economy_engine.csv") |> filter(engine_name == E)
econ |>
  transmute(NAICS = naics, Industry = label,
            `Employment in region` = scales::comma(region_emp),
            Establishments = scales::comma(region_est),
            `Share of US employment` = scales::percent(region_share_of_us, 0.1),
            `Employment LQ` = lq_emp) |>
  kable(align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r"))
```

Industries related to the Engine's technology (chosen from the NSF abstract, see `data/manual/engine_naics.csv`). County Business Patterns 2023; LQ = the industry's share of regional employment relative to its share of US employment (1 = US average). Region: `r econ$counties[1]`.

## Technology profile

```{r profile-text, results = "asis"}
if (V == "v1") {
  cat(sprintf("Version 1. The profile has %d statements. Item 1 comes from the grant title, the rest from the technical part of the NSF abstract. Each statement is mapped to one OpenAlex topic and to CPC codes.\n\n", nrow(profile)))
} else {
  cat(sprintf("Version 3.1, core. The NSF abstract names %d technologies of this Engine (scientific and technical fragments extracted with a fixed prompt; the extraction was done by hand in a chat session, not reproducible). For each technology, all 4,516 OpenAlex topics and all CPC main groups are ranked by several independent signals; the core keeps up to 2 topics and 2 CPC main groups per technology. *Judge*: chosen by a rubric judge where no candidate was confirmed by two kinds of evidence (also by hand in a chat session). An empty cell: no suitable item among the candidates. See [Methodology](../methodology.html) and the [comparison of versions](../compare.html).\n\n",
              n_distinct(profile$tech_id)))
}
```

```{r profile}
if (V == "v1") {
  profile |>
    transmute(`#` = item, Source = source, Statement = statement, `OpenAlex topic` = topic,
              Subfield = subfield, CPC = cpc) |>
    kable()
} else {
  fmt <- \(id, title, basis) paste0(id, " ", title, if_else(str_starts(basis, "judge"), " (judge)", ""))
  items <- profile |> filter(in_core) |> mutate(txt = fmt(item_id, item_title, basis))
  profile |> distinct(tech_id, tech_label) |>
    left_join(items |> filter(kind == "oa") |> group_by(tech_id) |>
                summarise(topics = paste(txt, collapse = "<br>"), .groups = "drop"), by = "tech_id") |>
    left_join(items |> filter(kind == "cpc") |> group_by(tech_id) |>
                summarise(cpc = paste(txt, collapse = "<br>"), .groups = "drop"), by = "tech_id") |>
    arrange(tech_id) |>
    transmute(`#` = tech_id, Technology = tech_label, `OpenAlex topics` = coalesce(topics, ""),
              `CPC main groups` = coalesce(cpc, "")) |>
    kable(escape = FALSE)
}
```

## People

```{r roles}
people |>
  count(Role = role_suggested) |> arrange(desc(n)) |> kable(col.names = c("Role", "People"))
```

```{r people-table}
people |>
  arrange(factor(role_suggested, c("researcher", "research_admin", "corporate_rd", "organizer")), name) |>
  transmute(Name = name, Role = role_suggested,
            `On NSF award` = if_else(in_nsf, coalesce(role_nsf, ""), ""),
            Title = str_trunc(coalesce(title_site, ""), 60),
            Organisation = str_trunc(coalesce(org_site, ""), 40),
            `Works since window (in Engine topics)` = case_when(
              !is.na(n_listed) ~ sprintf("[%d](publications.html#works-%s) (%d)", n_listed, person_id, n_topic),
              coalesce(reliable, FALSE) & !coalesce(check_merged, FALSE) ~ "0",
              coalesce(reliable, FALSE) ~ as.character(works_5y),
              TRUE ~ "-"),
            `h-index` = if_else(coalesce(reliable, FALSE), as.character(h_index), "-"),
            `Patents 2021-25 (in Engine profile)` = if_else(
              is.na(n_pat), "",
              sprintf("[%d](patents.html#patents-%s) (%d)", n_pat, person_id, n_pat_profile)),
            Site = if_else(is.na(site_url), "", sprintf("[page](%s)", site_url)),
            OpenAlex = if_else(coalesce(reliable, FALSE) & !coalesce(check_merged, FALSE) & !is.na(oa_id),
                               sprintf("[profile](https://openalex.org/%s)", oa_id), "")) |>
  kable()
```

Publication counts are shown only where the OpenAlex author matches both the name and the person's current organisation. The OpenAlex link is given only for these reliable matches, and not for profiles flagged as possibly merging several namesakes. *Site* links to the page of the Engine's website where the person is named. Click a number of works to see the list on the [Publications](publications.html) page. *Patents*: US grants 2021-2025 with the person among the inventors (same last and first name, address in the Engine's states); click the number for the list on the [Patents](patents.html) page. In brackets: works in the Engine's topics, patents with a CPC code in the Engine's technology profile.


## Researchers at partner organisations

```{r partner-researchers, results = "asis"}
pr_file <- proc_path("partner_researchers.csv")
pr <- if (file.exists(pr_file)) read_csv(pr_file, show_col_types = FALSE) |> filter(engine_name == E) else tibble()
if (nrow(pr)) {
  pr |>
    transmute(`#` = rank,
              Researcher = sprintf("[%s](https://openalex.org/%s)%s", name, author_id, if_else(in_team, " (team)", "")),
              Partner = partners,
              `Works in the Engine's topics` = works_in_topics,
              Citations = citations,
              Years = if_else(first_year == last_year, as.character(first_year), paste0(first_year, "-", last_year)),
              `Most cited of these works` = sprintf("[%s](https://openalex.org/%s)", str_trunc(top_work, 60), top_work_id)) |>
    kable() |> print()
  cat("\nThe grant names mostly managers; the technology is often developed at the partner universities and labs. These are the authors with the most works in the Engine's OpenAlex topics written at a knowledge-producer partner in the Engine's states, since the window start (at least 3 works; top 15). The list depends on the technology profile version. OpenAlex sometimes merges namesakes into one author: check the profile before relying on a name.\n")
} else cat("No knowledge-producer partner in the Engine's states with works in its topics.\n")
```

```{r papers-year, fig.height=3.5}
if (nrow(wyear)) {
  wyear |> filter(year >= as.integer(format(as.Date(eng$window_from), "%Y"))) |>
    pivot_longer(c(works, works_in_region), names_to = "set", values_to = "n") |>
    mutate(set = recode(set, works = "All partner institutions", works_in_region = "With an in-region partner")) |>
    ggplot(aes(year, n, colour = set)) + geom_line(linewidth = 1) + geom_point() +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Papers", colour = NULL) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
} else cat("No knowledge-producer partners with an OpenAlex institution record.")
```

```{r papers-partners}
if (nrow(wi)) {

    filter(partners_on_work != "") |>

}
```

```{r patents-year, fig.height=3.5}
pyear |> ggplot(aes(grant_year, patents)) + geom_col(fill = "#2c7fb8") +

```

```{r lq, fig.height=3.5}
if (nrow(lq)) {
  lq |> mutate(cpc = reorder(cpc, lq)) |>
    ggplot(aes(lq, cpc)) + geom_col(fill = "#41ab5d") + geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = 2) +

}
```

```{r assignees}
top_asg |> transmute(Assignee = assignee, `Regional patents in profile` = n) |> kable()
```

Partner-owned patents invented in the region: `r m$pat_partner_region`, of which `r m$pat_partner_region_tech` (`r scales::percent(m$share_partner_region_in_tech, accuracy = 0.1)`) fall in the Engine's technology profile.

## Competition

```{r comp-load}
comp_st <- rd("competition_states.csv") |> filter(engine_name == E)
comp_ct <- rd("competition_countries.csv") |> filter(engine_name == E)
comp_pp <- rd("competition_papers.csv") |> filter(engine_name == E)
reg_row <- comp_st |> filter(state == "ENGINE REGION")
```

With `r reg_row$patents` patents in the technology profile (2021-2025 grants), the Engine's region would rank **`r reg_row$rank_patents`** among US states; its specialisation (LQ) is `r reg_row$lq`.

```{r comp-states, fig.height=4.5}
comp_st |> filter(state != "ENGINE REGION") |> slice_max(patents, n = 12) |>
  bind_rows(reg_row |> mutate(state = "Engine region")) |>
  mutate(state = reorder(state, patents), own = state == "Engine region" | in_engine_states) |>
  ggplot(aes(patents, state, fill = own)) + geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("LQ %.2f", lq)), hjust = -0.1, size = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#e6550d", `FALSE` = "#9ecae1"), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2))) +
  labs(x = "Patents in the technology profile, 2021-2025 grants", y = NULL,
       title = "Leading US states vs the Engine's region", subtitle = "Orange: the Engine's region and its state(s)")
```

```{r comp-countries}
left_join(
  comp_ct |> transmute(Country = country, `Share of US patents in profile` = scales::percent(share, 0.1)),
  comp_pp |> transmute(Country = country, `Share of world papers in topics` = scales::percent(share, 0.1)),
  by = "Country") |>
  head(10) |> kable()
```

Patents: inventor countries on US grants in the profile (a patent counts for every country of its inventors). Papers: author countries of OpenAlex works in the Engine's topics since the window start.

## Data and limitations

- People: PIs and Co-PIs from the NSF Award API; leadership listed on the Engine's website. Roles come from titles and organisations, revised with OpenAlex evidence.
- Partners: as listed on the Engine's website, plus organisations of team members. Some Engines publish partner logos without names.
- Region: the Engine's counties where the list is known (NEO-SMART: 18 Northeast Ohio counties; STELLAR: 11 counties from the NSF abstract), otherwise its states (state-level proxy).
- Technology profile: `r PROFILE_LABELS[[V]]` (switch versions in the header). Partner papers and regional patents depend on it: v1 uses mostly CPC subclasses, the v3.1 core uses CPC main groups, which are narrower, so it counts fewer patents and the LQ of a small region rests on few patents.
- Papers: OpenAlex; partner papers are restricted to the Engine's OpenAlex topics.
- Patents: USPTO grants 2021-2025; inventor locations from PatentsView; pre-grant publications are not included.
